Sept 2026

Back in the Emergency Department: an update from nurse Leah Prairie

Three months into a three-year term of volunteer service, registered nurse Leah Prairie is settling back into clinical work in Kisiizi’s Emergency Department, alongside teaching, research support, and community life around the hospital. One recent highlight: Blessing, a baby found abandoned shortly after birth and nursed back to health at Kisiizi after arriving critically ill, is now nearly four months old, growing and much loved by staff and neighbours alike.

28 Aug 2026

Welcome, Dr Viola: a new full-time physician joins Kisiizi

Thank you to everyone who prayed and stood with Kisiizi through the physician shortage in Internal Medicine earlier this year — Dr Viola has now joined the hospital as a new full-time physician, restoring cover to the department. This also allows Kisiizi to resume training interns in this area. More about Dr Viola to follow.

28 Aug 2026

Empower milestone: nearly 11,000 girls reached

The Empower menstrual-health programme has now reached nearly 11,000 girls across schools near Kisiizi — up from just over 4,000 — through reusable pad packs sewn by local tailors, paired with menstrual health education in the classroom.

5 Aug 2026

Friends of Kisiizi Day — Saturday 3 October 2026

Friends of Kisiizi invites all supporters to a get-together at Brookside Church, Earley, Reading (RG6 7HG), 10am–4pm — hearing updates from Kisiizi and praying together for its future. No need to book: just bring a packed lunch, and refreshments are provided. Dr Medard Bitekyerezo (“Dr Biteks”), the Board’s new Chairman of Governors, is hoped to attend as Guest of Honour.

Advance notice: the hospital’s Platinum Jubilee celebrations are scheduled for 21–23 January 2028, in Kisiizi.

July 2026

Malnutrition Project: July report from the nutrition team

Community follow-up visits, health education and play therapy for malnourished children, alongside the income-generating farm projects — chickens, dairy, fish and garden — that help fund their care.

Malnutrition Project Report · July 2026

Our heartfelt gratitude goes out to our dear friends, partners, and stakeholders for the support rendered towards our clients and the wider community in the betterment of their health. A very big thank-you for your compassion, support, kindness, valuable insight, and time given in support of our malnourished clients and community.

Community visits

The team carried out individual follow-up visits in the community through July, supporting children previously managed on the ward for severe acute malnutrition and nutritional oedema — providing nutrition education, linking families to their local Village Health Team, and advising on hospital review where needed. Ongoing community activities also included health education on proper feeding recommendations, and play therapy.

This month at a glance
Health education talks16 talks · 91 attendees
Cooking demonstrations60 demonstrations · 19 attendees
Play therapy4 sessions / week
Demonstration gardenOngoing · free produce for needy patients
Income-generating projects

Alongside clinical care, the nutrition project runs four small income-generating projects that help fund care for malnourished clients.

  • Chicken: minimum flock numbers maintained; hatching services promoted, with one client engaged. Next month: continue vaccination, feeding and deworming.
  • Dairy: milk production fell by 11.3 L this month, due to prolonged drought reducing pasture and mating being carried out. Next month: pasture maintenance and veterinary follow-ups continue.
  • Fish: 114,000 UGX in income this month; the pond was maintained and fishing continues.
  • Garden: matooke income of 52,000 UGX (with two bunches given freely to a family in need), sugar cane income of 9,000 UGX, and vegetable income of 54,000 UGX. Next month: more mulching, weeding, and new vegetable seedlings.
Project finances
Total costsJune 1,485,300 · July 2,056,880 UGX
Income from farm produceJune 343,500 · July 640,000 UGX
Value of items given freelyJune 359,260 · July 315,980 UGX
Challenges
  • Insufficient land for the banana plantation — new land has been requested; response awaited.
  • Inadequate financial sustainability to run the project fully and support all malnourished clients in the hospital and surrounding communities.
  • Insufficient staff to complete project tasks within an appropriate timeframe.
  • Unstable RUTF supply from government stores, disrupting client care and progress.
  • Clients’ financial constraints — some request discharge before reaching targets, and some default on follow-up.
Looking ahead
  • Expansion of the nutrition project, pending feedback from hospital administration.
  • Community sensitisation involving community health extension workers.
  • Four community visits, twenty health education talks, seven cooking demonstrations, and daily play therapy reinitiated.
  • Seedlings from the demonstration garden distributed during follow-up visits.

In summary, the malnutrition project team has worked tirelessly to provide the best care to our clients. Follow-up visits in the community are not easy, as clients are often hard to reach — but it remains very important to visit those who have defaulted or who find it difficult to reach the hospital due to financial hardship, as these are often the clients who need our support the most. As always, we are happy to receive any feedback from you.

“Whoever oppresses the poor shows contempt for their Maker, but whoever is kind to the needy honors God.”Proverbs 14:31

21 Nov 2025

Dr Helen Allott receives an MBE

Chair of Trustees for Kisiizi Partners and a 36-year NHS veteran, Dr Helen — who first visited Kisiizi in 1999 — and her husband Alan were both recognised in the New Year Honours for their work with disadvantaged children abroad. Their charity has funded a new surgical ward.

12 Feb 2024

Baby Angel: a story of hope

An abandoned newborn, found under a pile of wood in a nearby forest, was brought to the Special Care Baby Unit and nursed back to health. She was later welcomed permanently into a family — and, staff hope, will grow up knowing she was loved by the whole Kisiizi community.
